items.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
items.summary: This is the first time European leaders have had direct communication with Russia's president in more than a year.
items.content:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - a rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.

The aim was looking at "future negotiations to help to end the war" in Ukraine, the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said. Their initiative was not on behalf of "Europe as a whole".

After the call, Putin said "confrontational" EU and Nato policies were prolonging the war which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken to the two Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin. Last week, Zelensky met them as well as US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.

The Ukrainian leader said he was grateful for the "active support" of his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts.

Tuesday's 90-minute phone call was held from the Finnish capital Helsinki, and showed "big differences in views", Støre said.

Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the call to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.

The call was "frank and substantive", Stubb said, explaining that the war's outcome will "have a direct impact on our and the broader European security".

Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."

The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.

He - like Stubb and Støre - had agreed to continue their direct phone communication, the statement added.

Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push

Støre said all their allies had been informed of the call ahead of time.

Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "very sceptical" of Tuesday's dialogue, telling Danish broadcaster DR, it had not been "co-ordinated with any of the rest of us".

Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates, was "moderately optimistic".

Relations between the US, Ukraine and its European allies have been souring since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia - allowing it to export oil to the US.

But last week, Stubb, Støre and Zelesnky met Witkoff in the Norwegian capital, before the US special envoy travelled on to St Petersburg to meet Putin.

Following the talks, Ukraine, Russia and the US agreed to resume three-way negotiations that Russia had stopped for months.

After speaking to the two Nordic leaders, Zelensky said part of their discussions with Putin had centred on November's trilateral talks to be held in Abu Dhabi.

Zelensky said he had discussed with them "various formats for our engagement with partners in Europe that could be useful in further supporting diplomacy, our defense, and our shared security".

Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.

As the US administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.

Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the European Union of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.

But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".

items.title: Gas serra fuori controllo: la CO2 raggiunge un nuovo record
items.summary: La CO2 tocca 426,8 ppm nel 2025. L'OMM avverte sui rischi per il clima e sugli altri gas serra.
items.content:
Non ci sono buone notizie sul fronte climatico, perché il nostro pianeta continua ad accumulare calore. A quanto pare il problema non riguarda soltanto le emissioni prodotte ogni anno, perché a preoccupare gli scienziati è soprattutto la quantità di gas serra che rimane nell'atmosfera. Queste, nello specifico, contribuiscono a trattenere energia e ad alimentare il riscaldamento globale per decenni, se non secoli.

A confermare questa tendenza è il nuovo bollettino dell'Organizzazione Meteorologica Mondiale (OMM), che fotografa una situazione tutt'altro che rassicurante. Nel 2025 la concentrazione media globale di anidride carbonica ha raggiunto 426,8 parti per milione (ppm), contro le 377,5 registrate nel 2004. Le misurazioni disponibili indicano inoltre che la crescita prosegue anche nel 2026.

Ma cerchiamo di capire cosa significa concretamente. Le parti per milione indicano quante molecole di CO2 sono presenti ogni milione di molecole d'aria, e anche aumenti apparentemente piccoli sono importanti, perché amplificano l'effetto serra e favoriscono l'accumulo di calore negli oceani e nell'atmosfera.

items.title: Bonus colonnine, fondi esauriti: sportello chiuso dopo circa 16.000 domande
items.summary: Le richieste presentate dal 22 settembre hanno esaurito le risorse disponibili per il 2026. Il contributo copre l’80% delle spese per l’acquisto e l’installazione di wallbox e colonnine domestiche ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Sono bastate circa 16.000 domande per esaurire i fondi del Bonus colonnine domestiche 2026. Il Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy ha disposto la chiusura anticipata dello sportello alle 12 di oggi, 27 ottobre, oltre tre mesi prima della scadenza originariamente prevista per il 31 gennaio 2027.

La ragione è l’esaurimento delle risorse finanziarie disponibili per l’annualità in corso. A partire dalla chiusura dello sportello non è quindi più possibile trasmettere nuove richieste per ottenere il contributo.

Le domande correttamente presentate prima delle 12 del 27 ottobre saranno ora esaminate secondo l’ordine cronologico di arrivo e potranno essere ammesse nei limiti dei fondi ancora effettivamente disponibili.

Il Bonus colonnine domestiche è l’incentivo promosso dal Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy e gestito da Invitalia per sostenere l’acquisto e l’installazione di infrastrutture di ricarica private per veicoli elettrici.

La dotazione complessiva prevista dal programma ammonta a 68 milioni di euro distribuiti su più anni. Per il 2026 sono stati stanziati 15 milioni di euro, cifra evidentemente già coperta dalle richieste arrivate poco più di un mese dopo l’apertura dello sportello, avvenuta il 22 settembre. Altri 15 milioni sono previsti per ciascuno degli anni dal 2027 al 2029, mentre per il 2030 la dotazione scenderà a 8 milioni.

L’incentivo copre l’80% delle spese ammissibili, fino a un massimo di 1.500 euro nel caso delle persone fisiche e di 8.000 euro per le installazioni realizzate sulle parti comuni dei condomìni.

Con la chiusura anticipata dello sportello è terminata quindi la fase di raccolta delle domande e comincia quella di verifica. Invitalia controllerà la completezza delle informazioni fornite, la correttezza formale delle richieste e la documentazione allegata. La concessione del contributo avviene comunque entro il limite delle risorse disponibili e seguendo l’ordine cronologico di presentazione.

Chi ha già trasmesso una domanda può continuare a verificarne lo stato accedendo all’area riservata della piattaforma dedicata.

Il Ministero lascia inoltre aperta la possibilità di una successiva riapertura dello sportello. Potrebbe accadere nel caso in cui tornassero disponibili risorse, per esempio a seguito di domande non ammesse o di economie maturate durante l’istruttoria. In quel caso termini e modalità verrebbero comunicati attraverso un nuovo avviso sui siti del Ministero e di Invitalia.

items.title: F1, Kimi Antonelli a un passo dalla gloria mondiale: in arrivo un incasso stellare
items.summary: Il bolognese della Mercedes sta per ricevere una somma extra per la conquista del Mondiale. Scopriamo come funzionano i bonus in F1.
items.content:
Kimi Antonelli potrà festeggiare persino arrivando fuori dalla zona punti nella prossima tappa in Messico qualora Russell o Hamilton non dovessero vincere la sfida. Con il trionfo di Austin l'italiano si è assicurato un posto nel firmamento della massima categoria del Motorsport, arrivando a un passo dal diventare il primo italiano dai tempi di Alberto Ascari a laurearsi campione del mondo di Formula 1 e il più giovane pilota a conquistare un titolo mondiale.Scaramanzie a parte, a soli 20 anni, compiuti lo scorso 25 agosto, Andrea Kimi Antonelli romperà un tabù che per il Belpaese dura da 73 anni per l'esattezza. Se non accadrà in Messico il numero 12 festeggerà in Brasile nella città del suo idolo Ayrton Senna. I piloti di F1 non ricevono dei premi da Liberty Media, ma possono vedersi assegnati dai team specifici bonus legati al piazzamento in classifica e alle vittorie conquistate. Si tratta di somme variabili che possono rendere molto ricchi i campioni del mondo. Nel 2024, ad esempio, Max Verstappen per la conquista del suo quarto riconoscimento iridato, condito da 9 successi e 14 podi, ricevette dalla Red Bull Racing una somma di 15 milioni di dollari solo per i bonus legati alle prestazioni, oltre allo stipendio base di 60 milioni di dollari.

Futuro Paperone

Non vi aspettate cifre simili per un ragazzo che ha corso appena 2 annate in F1, ma grazie alle sue numerose vittorie nel 2026 Kimi percepirà di sicuro svariati milioni extra da parte di Mercedes. Il salario base del bolognese, secondo quanto riportato sulle colonne di Racingnews365, è stimato intorno ai 2 milioni di dollari (circa 1,7 milioni di euro). Inoltre, va valutata la fetta di sponsor enorme che ha ottenuto e acquisirà in futuro il ragazzo, da sempre un elemento chiave dei ricavi dei driver di F1.Motorsportmagazine.com ha rivelato che la F1 ha generato un fatturato di 3,9 miliardi di dollari nel 2025 registrando un utile operativo, prima degli ammortamenti, pari a 946 milioni di dollari. Grazie a tali ricavi, i team hanno ricevuto complessivamente circa 1,4 miliardi di dollari, l'11% in più rispetto a quanto incassato nel 2024 quando i soldi ottenuti ammontavano a 1 miliardo e 266 milioni. Per questo motivo la conquista del primo posto della graduatoria costruttori ha una incidenza fondamentale anche nei bonus dei piloti. Antonelli e Russell non avranno problemi, salvo miracolose rimonte dei ferraristi, a conquistare il titolo.[caption id="attachment_292720" align="alignnone" width="1200"] Stipendio Kimi Antonelli Mercedes[/caption]

Mercedes comanda

Nella passata stagione Ferrari e Mercedes hanno ottenuto dei ricavi molto simili. La Scuderia modenese, grazie al bonus di partecipazione storica, ha incassato 222 milioni di euro contro i 218,7 milioni di euro ricevuti, da Mercedes. Nel 2026 il team anglotedesco potrebbe sforare i 230-235 milioni di euro. Una somma impressionante che favorirà anche il bolognese.Partendo dal presupposto che Forbes ha stimato che Lando Norris, iridato nel 2025, abbia avuto circa 10 milioni di dollari di bonus dalla McLaren per i meriti sportivi, riteniamo che Kimi possa ricevere una somma complessiva nel 2026 intorno ai 12 milioni di dollari, ovvero 10,7 milioni di euro. Il portale Sport e Finanza ha ipotizzato che la Mercedes, in caso di doppio riconoscimento, possa attribuire ad Antonelli una cifra totale di 14 milioni di dollari, ovvero 12,5 milioni di euro. Un importo assolutamente meritato per anche i pochi danni fatti in pista alle monoposto della Stella a tre punte.

items.title: Giving chat feedback gives Anthropic your data
items.summary: Article URL: https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996868-is-my-data-used-for-model-training Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50259406 Points: 94 # Comments: 49
items.content:
This article is about our commercial products such as Claude for Work and the Anthropic API. For our consumer products such as Claude Free, Pro, Max and when accounts from those plans use Claude Code, see here .

By default, we will not use your inputs or outputs from our commercial products (e.g. Claude for Work, Anthropic API, Claude Gov, etc.) to train our models.

If you explicitly report feedback or bugs to us (e.g. via our thumbs up/down feedback button), or otherwise choose to allow us to use your data, then we may use your chats and coding sessions to train our models.

To find out more information regarding your use of an Anthropic commercial offering, or if you would like to know how to contact us regarding a privacy related topic, see our Trust Center and Commercial Terms .

When you provide us feedback via our thumbs up / down button, we will store the entire related conversation, including any content, custom styles, conversation preferences, or model settings, in our secured back-end for up to 5 years. Feedback data does not include raw content from connectors (e.g. Google Drive), including remote and local MCP servers, though data may be included if it’s directly copied into your conversation with Claude.

We de-link your feedback from your user and customer IDs before it’s used by Anthropic. We may use your feedback to analyze the effectiveness of our services, conduct research, study user behavior, and train our AI models as permitted under applicable laws. We do not combine your feedback with your other conversations with Claude.

Here’s an example of what you’ll see when using the thumbs up/thumbs down button to provide a feedback report from claude.ai:

items.title: PHP2Shell: Exploitation Attempts and Remediation Trends
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-exploitation-so-far Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50259343 Points: 106 # Comments: 39
items.content:
Last week, we published a report describing two major vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619). Since then, alongside much of the security industry, the Wiz Research team has been monitoring for related activity in the wild and reviewing publicly available exploit code. So far, we have observed a limited number of exploitation attempts in our telemetry and have not identified a publicly available proof of concept (PoC) demonstrating complete, general end-to-end exploitation against an arbitrary target. Some partners have, however, privately disclosed to us exploits that work against a variety of targets and we continue to experiment internally. Videos demonstrating our successful exploitations are available at php2shell.com .

This post summarizes what we have observed in terms of remediation efforts and exploitation attempts across real world environments and in our own honeypot data to date and shares findings from our ongoing investigation into these activities.

We will continue monitoring developments and update this post as new evidence emerges.

Following PHP2Shell’s public disclosure on October 21, 2026, Wiz telemetry has recorded an approximate 67% decrease in the daily number of distinct Internet-exposed machines vulnerable to PHP2Shell over the past few days. Separately, among vulnerable Internet-exposed machines, the proportion running PHP version 7.3 or earlier fell from 8.3% to 5.7% over a period of five days. This measures the share of the observed population running older versions that did not receive official backports.

During this period, the number of significantly affected organizations - defined here as those with at least one exposed and vulnerable instance - fell by approximately 47.9% (see graph below). For reference, our data shows that PHP itself is in use by 65% of organizations in our dataset.

Together, these observations are consistent with organizations collectively reducing their exposure through a combination of patching, upgrading, retiring affected machines and restricting internet access (note that this data shows the overall trend, but does not establish the relative contribution of each remediation strategy; scan coverage and size of observed population can also affect the overall reported numbers over time).

We have so far observed the following types of activities in this context:

Attempts using the PHP2Shell exploit mechanism, with techniques matching those of public PoCs .

PHP2Shell-branded tools unrelated to the vulnerabilities that instead relied on session poisoning and a separate local file inclusion (LFI) vulnerability in the application.

We observed two variants of an open source exploit kit targeting PHP-based software. Neither completed the exploit chain in the attempts we captured. The older variant encountered request-size limits or failed to produce the expected memory-exhaustion condition. The newer variant did consistently exhaust PHP’s memory, but failed to obtain the memory addresses needed to continue.

The first request to our PHP-CGI honeypot came from 3.37.227[.]134 . It matched the kit’s older chain, found under archive/legacy-8m/exploit.py and its accompanying stage scripts. The first full exploit stage used a multipart body containing 1,005 parts, including a field named big filled with approximately 12 MB of padding:

According to the kit’s notes, this stage attempts to exhaust memory during a session reset, leaving the session state available for a later request.

On our honeypot, it failed before reaching that code. The declared request size exceeded the configured 8 MB post_max_size limit, so PHP skipped processing the multipart body and logged:

The author has since moved this chain into the kit’s archive directory.

In a later attempt, 103.151.172[.]95 sent a longer sequence from the legacy chain. It included stalled connections intended to occupy other Apache workers.

When only one worker was available the exploit attempted heap-shaping by sending requests containing 1,001 fields of 3,000 bytes each. These requests didn’t trigger the memory exhaustion flow required. So there is no evidence that this attempt reached the intended memory-exhaustion condition.

Most IP addresses we captured used the newer chain, built from pure/mk_a1.py and pure/mk_leak_b.py . We observed this variant in multiple attempts.

This variant progressed further: its first stage consistently caused PHP to exhaust its memory. The following stage, which attempts to leak process memory, failed in every run we captured.

The server logged a fatal error indicating that PHP reached its limit, for example:

The chain depends on consecutive exploit requests reaching the same Apache child process. To increase the chances of that happening, the kit attempts to occupy the other workers with incomplete requests. Each connection declares a large body, sends a single byte and stalls:

One address, 178.249.214[.]6 , opened 399 of these connections alongside 400 GET requests before sending the exploit stages. The address is a VPN exit node, which limits what we can infer about the source.

A1 is a chunked multipart request containing a null-byte session ID, 860 empty file parts with long, deeply nested array names and several groups of padding fields:

The request is designed to exhaust memory during session handling at a point that can leave the session ID pointing to freed memory.

Every A1 request we captured returned HTTP 500, accompanied by a PHP error matching:

This confirms that A1 reached the intended memory-exhaustion condition on our honeypot. It does not, by itself, confirm that the stale session state needed by the next stage was preserved.

B1 followed roughly a second later. It sent another chunked multipart request containing PHPSESSID=a , PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS=k0 and two large padding fields.

The failed leaks highlight a broader challenge: building a generalized exploit that works reliably across PHP versions and deployment configurations is difficult. The kit’s B1 layout was calculated for the official php:8.4.26-apache image with a 128 MB memory limit. Other instances like our Roundcube honeypot ran the same PHP version from a different build, with additional extensions and a 64 MB memory limit. These differences can affect heap layout and memory reuse, potentially preventing the leak from working as expected.

Reliable worker pinning adds another challenge. Consecutive exploit requests must reach the same Apache child process while the required session state persists. Request timeouts, network latency and worker availability can disrupt this sequence. In our own testing, request timeouts combined with network latency were enough to prevent the chain from completing over an internet connection.

So far, we have not identified a publicly available, generalized solution for either worker pinning or information leaking across different deployments. Simply copying public PoCs and running them at scale does not address the work needed to turn a configuration-specific exploit into a reliable operational kit. We expect these barriers to diminish over time: some threat actors have the expertise needed to adapt the chain and build more robust tooling.

We also saw failed exploitation attempts from 15.204.59[.]70 and 162.35.99[.]94 , but these scanners did successfully exploit Adel Karimi's honeypot , which was a likely contributing factor to CISA’s decision to include PHP2Shell in their KEV list .

We also observed tools labeled as PHP2Shell exploits that did not actually attempt to exploit either vulnerability. The earliest such traffic, from 85.11.187[.]35 , matched a Go port of “Chain A” from WoYinDao/CVE-2026-109618-CVSS-9.2-Critical .

The tool used a longstanding session-poisoning technique, attempting to write PHP code into a session file through the upload-progress feature. The request below is abbreviated:

It then attempted to execute that code by including the session file:

Crucially, lfi_sink.php is a vulnerable endpoint supplied by the PoC’s lab environment. The tool assumes that this endpoint exists on the target; without it or an equivalent local file inclusion (LFI) vulnerability, the chain cannot execute code.

A padded variant triggered our memory-exhaustion detection, but we observed no successful code execution. Despite the PHP2Shell branding, this activity relied on an unrelated technique and a vulnerable application endpoint.

We have not yet observed successful end-to-end PHP2Shell exploitation in our own telemetry. However, Adel Karimi’s public report and supporting data provide the most robust public evidence we have seen to date, correlating exploit traffic, memory disclosure and subsequent code execution on his honeypots. Notably, those targets used a favorable single-worker Apache mod_php configuration, so the findings do not establish reliability across other deployments.

Our observations show that triggering memory exhaustion alone is not enough to complete the exploit chain. Differences in PHP builds, memory limits and worker behavior can prevent subsequent stages from working. The challenge for opportunistic attackers is turning currently available public PoCs into similarly reliable operational tooling or developing it on their own. In our view, PHP2Shell remains a risk in both the short and long term and applying the PHP security updates or remediating through other means therefore remains essential.

items.title: I leader di Finlandia e Norvegia sentono Putin. Le critiche della premier danese
items.summary: Store: la telefonata è durata 90 minuti, gli alleati Ue erano stati informati. Poi hanno sentito Zelensky. Fonti di Palazzo Chigi: l'Ue scelga chi la rappresenta su Kiev, non vada in ordine sparso
items.content:
Il presidente della Finlandia Alexander Stubb e il premier norvegese Jonas Gahr Store hanno avuto una conversazione telefonica con Vladimir Putin. Lo conferma la presidenza finlandese spiegando che "l'obiettivo della telefonata è stato portare un messaggio diretto a Putin in relazione ai futuro negoziati. La telefonata è legata al prossimo round di colloqui previsto ad Abu Dhabi". Stub e Store - viene spiegato - hanno parlato "in veste di leader dei rispettivi Paese, e non a nome dell'Europa ". "La discussione è stata franca e sostanziale", ha sottolineato Stubb.

"Siamo paesi confinanti con la Russia. L'esito di questa guerra avrà un impatto diretto sulla nostra sicurezza e su quella dell'Europa nel suo complesso. Per porre fine alla guerra sono necessari colloqui diretti", ha detto Stubb. "La guerra comporta enormi costi umani e materiali. Le sofferenze e la distruzione avranno ripercussioni su intere generazioni. Durante la telefonata abbiamo sottolineato l'importanza di un allentamento delle tensioni", ha dichiarato Store. I due hanno parlato da Helsinki.

La telefonata con Putin di Stubb e Store che "hanno subito voluto precisare di aver parlato a nome delle rispettive nazioni e non dell'Europa" dimostra che "bisogna designare al più presto, e in modo condiviso, una o più personalità con un chiaro mandato a parlare a nome dell'Europa" per "tutelarne al meglio gli interessi e la sicurezza". Lo fanno sapere fonti di Palazzo Chigi, sottolineando che Giorgia Meloni ha "un rapporto di grande stima" coi due "alla guida di due nazioni che confinano con la Russia e hanno sempre sostenuto l'Ucraina". Ma, aggiungono le stesse fonti, "il negoziato non aspetta: l'Europa non può permettersi di perdere ulteriore terreno, deve decidere chi la rappresenta e deve farlo rapidamente , non può continuare a muoversi in ordine sparso e in formati che mutano di settimana in settimana, pena la progressiva perdita di peso nel negoziato".

Questa telefonata, osservano fonti di Palazzo Chigi, "dice soprattutto, e in maniera chiara, una cosa: in Europa non si è ancora trovato un accordo su chi debba rappresentare gli interessi del continente europeo nel processo di pace. È proprio questo vuoto a spingere le singole nazioni a muoversi su base nazionale". Gli stessi Stubb e Store "hanno subito voluto precisare di aver parlato a nome delle rispettive nazioni e non dell'Europa. Non potevano fare altrimenti, perché oggi nessuno può farlo". Ed è "per questa ragione - aggiungono le stesse fonti - che l'Italia sostiene da tempo che bisogna designare al più presto" uno o più rappresentanti per Kiev. E il governo italiano "è pronto a continuare a fare la sua parte perché questa scelta avvenga in tempi brevi".

Nel corso della conversazione con i leader di Finlandia e Norvegia, il presidente russo Vladimir Putin ha valutato la situazione attuale nella zona di conflitto in Ucraina, ricordandone le cause profonde, ha riferito l'ufficio stampa del Cremlino, citato da Tass. Putin ha osservato che una pace giusta e duratura in Ucraina è possibile solo se si tiene conto degli interessi della Russia e ha inoltre discusso con le controparti delle garanzie di sicurezza nel Mar Baltico e nell'Europa settentrionale. I leader hanno ribadito l'importanza di sostenere il diritto marittimo internazionale e il principio della libertà di navigazione.

"È stato sottolineato che il raggiungimento di una pace giusta e duratura è possibile solo con la piena e incondizionata considerazione dei legittimi interessi della Federazione Russa ", si legge nella dichiarazione del Cremlino.

"Ho parlato con il presidente finlandese e con il primo ministro norvegese a seguito della loro telefonata odierna con il leader russo e in prosecuzione delle nostre discussioni tenutesi a Oslo con i rappresentanti degli Stati Uniti, dell'Europa e della NATO. Sono grato per l'esauriente aggiornamento e per questa iniziativa". Così Volodymyr Zelensky su Telegram. Secondo Zelensky, i leader di Finlandia e Norvegia hanno chiaramente detto a Putin che "sono necessari veri passi di de-escalation verso l'allentamento delle tensioni per quanto riguarda la nostra energia e le nostre infrastrutture".

La premier danese Mette Frederiksen ha criticato la scelta di Stubb e Store di agire "per conto proprio" telefonando a Putin. "Sono molto scettica riguardo a questa iniziativa norvegese e finlandese. Non è stata concordata con nessuno di noi", ha dichiarato ai giornalisti a margine di un incontro tra i leader dei paesi nordici - tra cui Store e Stubb - in Finlandia. "Onestamente, non so cosa pensino di poter ottenere quei due paesi con questa mossa", ha aggiunto.

Store ha dichiarato che la telefonata di questa mattina con Vladimir Putin è durata circa 90 minuti. " Tutti i partner e le nazioni alleate sono stati informati prima della telefonata", ha affermato dopo che la premier danese ha criticato la mossa. Store ha sollecitato una de-escalation nella guerra in Ucraina e ha affermato che le sue opinioni e quelle del presidente finlandese Alexander Stubb erano in linea con la Coalizione dei Volenterosi, un gruppo di oltre 30 paesi che si sono impegnati a fornire garanzie di sicurezza all'Ucraina.

Stubb e Store hanno partecipato a colloqui con la delegazione ucraina e l'inviato speciale di Donald Trump, Steve Witkoff, a Oslo la scorsa settimana . Witkoff ha poi incontrato Vladimir Putin a San Pietroburgo.

items.title: Hypatia, da una piccola pietra una storia inattesa del Sistema solare
items.summary: Diversa da quella ricostruita dai meteoriti finora noti
items.content:
Hypatia , una piccola pietra scura di origine extraterrestre , rinvenuta nel deserto egiziano , potrebbe conservare tracce di materiali risalenti agli albori del Sistema Solare o a un periodo precedente la sua formazione, e raccontarne una storia inattesa . E' quanto emerge dallo studio sul campione, che porta il nome della matematica, astronoma e filosofa greca a capo della scuola neoplatonica di Alessandria nel IV Secolo d.C. La ricerca è pubblicata sulla rivista Space Science Reviews da Luca Bindi, dell'Università di Firenze, anche presidente del consiglio scientifico della Fondazione Parsec, e Marco Morelli, del Museo italiano di Scienze planetarie - Fondazione Parsec e associato dell'Istituto Nazionale di Astrofisica, assieme a Marco A.G. Andreoli della University of the Witwatersrand (Sudafrica). Dalla ricerca è emerso che Hypatia ha caratteristiche difficili da ricondurre ai gruppi di meteoriti conosciute : è composta prevalentemente da carbonio , è quasi priva di silicati (i minerali più abbondanti nella crosta terrestre) e presenta una struttura ricca di diamante . "Hypatia - si legge nell'articolo - rappresenta un caso di studio unico e rivoluzionario in cosmochimica , che mette in discussione le ipotesi fondamentali sulla natura e la diversità dei materiali solidi nel Sistema solare primordiale ".

Ricostruendo e valutando le evidenze mineralogiche, chimiche e isotopiche disponibili per confrontare le diverse ipotesi sulla sua origine, l'interpretazione proposta dai ricercatori è che Hypatia si sia formata dall'aggregazione di polveri eterogenee , in larga parte di origine interstellare , nelle prime fasi del Sistema solare . Successivi impatti tra corpi solidi protoplanetari in formazione avrebbero trasformato parte del carbonio in diamante , senza cancellare del tutto le differenze conservate al suo interno. Si tratta, osservano gli autori della ricerca, di un modello scientifico che cerca di spiegare l'insieme delle osservazioni, ma la storia precisa della pietra resta oggetto di ricerca . "Il caso di Hypatia - osservano i ricercatori - suggerisce che i materiali da cui si è formato il Sistema solare fossero assai diversi rispetto a quanto è possibile ricavare dallo studio delle meteoriti arrivate fino a noi . Aggregati ricchi di carbonio e fragili potrebbero essere stati più diffusi in passato, ma proprio la loro fragilità sarebbe alla base della minore possibilità di conservarsi".

items.title: Youssef Siher davanti al gip, sceglie di non rispondere. I legali: 'Torni libero'
items.summary: Per gli avvocati 'nessuna istigazione né terrorismo'. I pm chiedono che resti in carcere
items.content:
Si è avvalso della facoltà di non rispondere Youssef Siher, il creatore dei canali social del "Movimento 17 ottobre", interrogato nel carcere milanese di San Vittore dalla gip Tiziana Landoni.

"Lui non ha fatto niente. Non c'è stata alcuna condotta istigatoria alle violenze, non c'è il terrorismo, non c'è alcun reato e noi nell'udienza abbiamo contestato le imputazioni dal punto di vista del diritto", hanno spiegato i legali di Siher dopo l'udienza in carcere. Gli avvocati Benedetto Ciccarone e Yasmina Abu Sharar hanno chiesto alla giudice che il ricercatore torni libero.

Il 30enne è stato fermato il 24 ottobre per istigazione a delinquere aggravata dalla finalità di terrorismo e violenza organizzata nelle manifestazioni pubbliche, perché ritenuto l'amministratore dei canali social del "Movimento 17 ottobre", da lui creato subito dopo la guerriglia urbana in pieno centro a Milano.

La gip Tiziana Landoni, dopo l'udienza per ascoltare il giovane, difeso dall'avvocata Yasmina Abu Sharar e legato sia ai gruppi ProPal che all'antagonismo milanese, dovrà decidere sulla richiesta di convalida del fermo e di custodia cautelare in carcere avanzata dal procuratore Marcello Viola e dalla pm Francesca Crupi, presente all'udienza di convalida. Pm che hanno contestato come esigenze cautelari sia il pericolo di fuga che quello di reiterazione del reato. La decisione della giudice deve arrivare entro domani.

Per la procura, Siher ha dato "prova di conoscere gli strumenti informatici idonei a sviluppare la sua strategia rivoluzionaria, anche mediante la redazione di comunicati idonei a concentrare nelle piazze migliaia di persone pronte a tutto".

E i suoi messaggi su Instagram e sul gruppo Telegram, con oltre 11mila persone, sarebbero stati "una dichiarazione di 'guerra' continua (...) deliberatamente volta, e sicuramente idonea, a incutere un profondo timore nella popolazione e a destabilizzare l'ordinario corso della vita civile".

Un progetto "eversivo", di "rivoluzione contro l'attuale governo" e di sostegno "alla rivolta", che lui, secondo i pm, potrebbe portare ancora avanti sfruttando pure "il suo elevato background culturale ed i suoi contatti relazionali". Da qui la richiesta di carcere, anche perché altrimenti, grazie alla sua "rete relazionale", potrebbe fuggire "all'estero".

"Non indossate subito i passamontagna, altrimenti ci fermano prima". Era questa la prima regola del 'manuale di condotta' diramato sui social per evitare di essere identificati dalle forze dell'ordine e mandare a monte i piani, durante gli assalti al centro storico di Milano il 17 e 18 ottobre scorsi. A dare le istruzioni dettagliate su cosa indossare, come vestirsi e come muoversi per le strade di Milano era un minorenne residente in provincia di Monza, individuato dalla Digos della Questura brianzola nell'ambito delle indagini a seguito dei disordini.

Nel pomeriggio del 22 ottobre i poliziotti si sono presentati a casa sua, per dare esecuzione a un decreto di perquisizione emesso dalla Procura per i Minorenni di Milano. Nella sua camera gli agenti hanno trovato il passamontagna indicato nelle chat e capi d'abbigliamento che sarebbero stati saccheggiati in un negozio.

Propositi di aggressione agli agenti per sottrarre le armi di ordinanza, incendi a edifici pubblici ed esplicite indicazioni su come armarsi per scendere in piazza il 17 e 18 ottobre a Milano. È il quadro emerso dall'analisi dello smartphone del minorenne di Monza perquisito il 22 ottobre dalla Digos brianzola, che era risalita a lui intercettando in rete le sue indicazioni su come evitare l'identificazione durante i disordini milanesi. E' dal suo dispositivo, come è emerso nei giorni scorsi, che gli investigatori hanno scoperto un gruppo WhatsApp composto da oltre 230 partecipanti, nel quale venivano organizzate e pianificate nuove azioni violente su scala regionale in vista del 24 ottobre.

Nelle chat il 'manuale di condotta' non riguardava soltanto l'abbigliamento per eludere i controlli, ma conteneva istruzioni dettagliate su come muoversi in gruppo ed equipaggiarsi per lo scontro: "girate con qualcosa tipo coltelli per sicurezza", "portatevi mazze e bastoni", fino a indicazioni su dove reperire fumogeni e petardi ad alto potenziale.

Tra i messaggi scambiati tra i ragazzi compaiono anche espliciti incitamenti all'attacco diretto alle forze dell'ordine e alle istituzioni: "siamo tutti insieme contro la polizia", "prendiamone uno lo picchiamo e gli leviamo l'arma di dosso", fino all'ipotesi di "mandare a fuoco un edificio del governo". Nelle conversazioni non mancavano poi la programmazione di danneggiamenti ai mezzi di servizio ed esortazioni a compiere veri e propri saccheggi ai danni dei negozi.

items.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
items.summary: The France star had referred to the former Chinese leader as a "dictator" during an interview about memes.
items.content:
Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.

Mbappé had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement.

Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".

The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.

A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.

Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé.

The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's Aurélien Tchouaméni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, Mbappé does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".

The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".

Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.

But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to "a Chinese dictator".

Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people".

Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.

Chinese fans have been criticising Mbappé – who is popular in China and has huge brand endorsements – of "profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public".

"International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly," reads another comment on Weibo.

As the anger online grew louder, Chinese brands began to cut ties, although they did not explicitly refer to the video.

The country's largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people".

Drinks giant Dongpeng issued a similar statement: "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments."

According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, state broadcaster CCTV's news apps will not feature content related to the French striker. CCTV will also stop showing La Liga matches, Chinese media reported on Tuesday. Real Madrid is one of 20 clubs that play in the Spanish football league and is the most decorated team with 36 league titles.

China's foreign ministry has also weighed in, with spokesperson Lin Jian saying: "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."

China is a major market for international sports stars and homegrown brands have signed multimillion-dollar endorsement contracts with Mbappé, Norwegian striker Erling Haaland, and NBA player Stephen Curry.

By 14:00 local time on Tuesday, five of the top 10 trending topics on Weibo centered on Mbappé, with the hashtag "multiple brands terminate partnerships with Mbappé" topping the list.

"Don't ever come to China," read one of the top comments on Weibo.

Mao founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and ruled through tumultuous decades in the 1960s and 1970s.

His attempt at rapid industrialisation, which he called the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party.

His death in 1976 brought a new era for China, which began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao's rule, he continued to be hailed by the party as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach.

So jokes or memes about Mao are seen not just as an insult to the party but also its closely-guarded narrative about the country's past.

It's unclear when the Mbappé meme involving Mao began but his nickname, "the dictator", has made the striker the subject of many memes and jokes online.

Mbappé is widely regarded as one of the best footballers in the world and has wielded significant influence at the clubs he has played for. His extraordinary speed, goalscoring ability and worldwide popularity have made him a global icon, attracting millions of fans, major sponsorship deals and media attention, with his influence extending into fashion, culture and business.

In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop's sandwiches, leading to more jokes about the nickname.

France teammate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup, calling Mbappé Mobut – a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades.

In an interview with France Football in September, Mbappé acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they "sometimes reveal a lack of political and human awareness among people".

"There's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history," he said.

"Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life."

items.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton goes to auction in New York with £4.5m price tag
items.summary: The auction of the rare skeleton comes amid debate in the scientific community about whether dinosaur remains should end up in private hands or public view.
items.content:
The mounted skeleton of a newly-identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex is up for auction - with a price-tag of at least $6m (£4.5m).

Nicknamed "Jodi", the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton will be auctioned by Sotheby's in New York. The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus.

The Late Cretaceous carnivore is expected to fetch up to $9m when it goes under the hammer on Tuesday. The auction comes after Sotheby's sold a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed "Gus", for a record $50.1m (£37.4m) in July.

The sale comes as some in the scientific community debate whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately.

Sotheby's described "Jodi" as an "excellent exhibition-ready" skeleton with about 191 fossil-bone elements and a "beautifully preserved, virtually complete skull".

The auction house added that the Nanotyrannus is "one of only three such skeletons known to science." The specimen is the first to come to market since the existence of the genus was confirmed by US researchers last October, Sotheby's said.

Megan Jenkins, a palaeontologist at the University of Portsmouth, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Tuesday that Nanotyrannus "was for a very long time believed to be sort of a teenager of T. rex".

"But it's a lot smaller and its a lot more gracile. So it's very sort-of sleek, slender, [with] blade-like teeth for slicing through meat," Jenkins said.

Tyrannosaurus rex and Nanotyrannus lived alongside one another during the same geological period approximately 67 million years ago.

"Jodi" was initially exhibited as a juvenile T. rex at London's Frieze Masters international art fair in October 2023, before the Nanotyrannus genus was classified.

The skeleton was discovered in the US state of Montana by rancher Jodi Pierson on her land in the Hall Creek Formation, a heavily studied geological site. It was later excavated by commercial palaeontologist Clayton Phipps.

Phipps also discovered the famous "Dueling Dinosaurs" fossil. That specimen, which shows the remains of a Nanotyrannus and Triceratops apparently in combat, was found eight miles (13km) away from "Jodi" in 2006.

The "Dueling Dinosaurs" discovery became crucial to the research published by Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli that classified Nanotyrannus as separate from T. rex. Their paper ended decades of debate over whether the dinosaurs were distinct from one another.

The auction of "Jodi" comes as some scientists warn that auctions could herald a new era in fossil collecting by the ultra-rich.

Researchers told the BBC after the sale of "Gus" that such remains should be exhibited in public spaces where they can be more freely studied.

Prof Steve Brusatte, a palaeontologist at the University of Edinburgh and consultant on the Jurassic Park films, told BBC World Service's What in the World programme in July that the T. rex's auction was "concerning".

"I don't know of any museum or university that can afford a price tag like that," he said. "Imagine if the Mona Lisa was just owned by a super-wealthy person and it wasn't on display and people couldn't see it, couldn't enjoy it."

He said that the time that he hoped such a sale didn't become a trend, adding it could adversely affect scientific research and public education.

Responding to today's auction, Brusatte called it "harrowing" that "Jodi" could disappear from public view.

"We've really just found out that Nanotyrannus is real, and now one of the best skeletons is about to be sold to the highest bidder, and it's harrowing to think it could disappear into the vaults of a collector rather than displayed on a museum where it can wow and inspire kids and families and the public at large," he told the BBC.

But Jenkins told the Today programme on Tuesday there were two sides to the debate, and that a lot of time, effort and money went into excavating the specimens.

"I don't begrudge the people involved for wanting to sell it for such a large amount of money," she said. "Although its a scary prospect, actually a lot of them have ended up in the public eye... these things without a doubt will end end up in a museum at some point."

items.title: Here Be Monsters: What Do You Still Need to Know When Agents Do the Work?
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.adrq.dev/here-be-monsters-what-do-you-still-need-to-know-when-agents-do-the-work Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50258868 Points: 71 # Comments: 17
items.content:
CI was failing. This was unexpected. I have dialed in my agentic workflow to a point where I would be surprised if one of my agents committed a branch that had failing tests. Maybe it's a CI flake or environment issue? Wait, it's SonarQube complaining about App.tsx ? Did we pull in a new suspicious dependency from npm or something? Nope. SonarQube is flagging this file for cyclomatic complexity. Haven't seen that one in a while.

Yep. App.tsx consists of about 30 lines of code, except 15 of those lines are actually entire components that Codex decided to write each on a single line . That itself would be ok, just run it through prettier and we're done. But that doesn't explain the cyclomatic complexity. Each of these was a fairly involved component with a good amount of display and business logic. Old self would have carefully refactored it and made sure the code was readable . On the other hand, Codex didn't care that entire components were on a single line, and more importantly, it didn't mind the complexity. It had been happily and reliably iterating on that file through several features.

The CI tool was flagging an issue, perhaps correct, perhaps incorrect. But this is a real system so I had to dive in. After formatting the files, I went through and inspected the components and logic. Did Codex go beyond what a typical dev might have in terms of covering edge cases and did it slightly over-engineer it? Yes, but it was all correct . No complaints from me. All of the complexity was warranted by the business requirements. So I told Codex to make SonarQube happy, which it did by refactoring and splitting things up into 10 files. CI passed; things shipped. Although this particular incident had a quick resolution, you can probably imagine how it could have gone much worse. This was, after all, code I had never seen before.

This is where our industry is headed: Owning a software system will depend a lot less on having written it (or similar systems) by hand; instead, what will become most important is knowing just enough to know when something is wrong, and being willing and able to dive as deep as needed, when needed.

Imagine that you're on a boat (you decide what type of boat you like) and your job is to collect little nuggets of gold from the bottom of the ocean. Up until very recently, if you wanted to get your bag of gold you would need to jump into the water, swim to the bottom, look around, and stuff your bag. Easy peasy if you're in clear, shallow waters, but you can imagine how quickly this can escalate into something much more difficult. So as the shallow water mines started drying up, you and fellow engineers built all sorts of machinery and tooling to extract gold from ever deeper and more dangerous waters. This worked well for the most part, you and your team would carefully assemble, maintain, rotate the machinery and would constantly dive to the seabed mining operation to keep it running. Every so often you'd hear about the collapse of some mining operations, sometimes due to the sheer underwater pressure, other times through accidents, or operator incompetence. The challenge is that this is a very geologically active world, so the seabed keeps changing with some mines drying up and new ones popping up in different places.

Good news though! The last few years have seen the development of ever more sophisticated divebots that can go down and build a mining operation on their own. You just tell them where to build and off they dive and only surface to give you updates and gold nuggets. Things are great, you can now relax on your boat while your divebots do their thing and all you have to worry about is how much gold you can stuff into your boat. This is the Optimists camp.

"Wait till your divebots go too deep and get lost". "Haha your divebots brought you stuff that looks like gold but is actually shiny octopus poop". As the divebots proliferate you see more and more horror stories. Divebots getting lost and forgetting what they are supposed to be building. Divebots building something so complex and grotesque that they have trouble maintaining it, only for it to be discarded by the next generation of divebots. All of the underwater mining operations went from being carefully designed and engineered cathedrals to more like haphazard mansions, with hidden passages and horrors lurking. The more detached from the operation you are, the more spectacular the failures. This is the Skeptics camp.

The software engineering industry (and I suspect many other industries soon) is living through a version of the above scenario. You probably already know whether Skeptic or Optimist describes you better, even if you're still not sure which camp you want to commit to.

The traditional wisdom is that in order to develop and maintain a non-trivial system you need to have a proper working model of it. I think few people would argue with that. And in software engineering you would acquire that working model by working directly with the code. Years and decades of practice writing and reading code give you the knowledge and tools needed to understand the systems you're responsible for. Every production incident, every late-night debugging session, every successful release. All of these experiences give you the perspective needed to have ownership of a system. In the context of this post, ownership means you're the one who gets called when something breaks .

Agents (divebots) are turning all of that on its head. Divebots produce output much faster than anyone can absorb, and while in complex systems of the past you could assume that the code had at one point gone through the hands of a human, that is no longer true. It is now possible for experienced practitioners to manage fleets of divebots and create software at an unprecedented scale. These operators know the craft and bring their considerable experience to manage and architect large systems that would have taken teams to build in the past. But that exposes what's probably the biggest challenge facing our industry: how do we train the next generation of engineers?

At their extremes, the Optimists and the Skeptics have wildly different answers to this question. On the one hand you have reputable voices saying that the only way to maintain control of these systems is to read every line of code the divebots produce. Be able to code it by hand. Be able to explain what every piece of code does and how it fits into the context of the applications. In the other camp, you have equally reputable voices saying to not even bother looking at the code. Focus your energy on figuring out what to build and forget about how it is built. The models will handle it. I don't think either of these is right.

The fact is that the way that today's senior engineers learned, ie. through coding by hand, endless hours debugging, production incidents, etc. is not a path that is viable for juniors today. To be clear, it is not economically viable, meaning that it is highly unlikely that companies will be willing to sponsor juniors for years while they "learn to do it by hand". That's wishful thinking. An alternative that is often presented is the "make sure you understand every line your agent wrote" advice, or "pair with a senior", or "perform careful code reviews". Again, wishful thinking at all but perhaps a few shops. If you think that the industry at large will adopt these practices, I've got a bridge to sell you. Hit me up.

In order to figure out a viable path for achieving some measure of mastery, we have to look at what it means to own a non-trivial software system. If you think about your typical architect/lead/CTO and how they operate, it becomes clear that to be successful they need to have a model of the system in their head, a chart of the waters. The real question is at what level of granularity ? Imagine a legacy 1-million line codebase, it was written and expanded over the years by a number of people. The CTO may have even written parts of it. Now imagine there is a production issue and you're the unlucky SRE trying to figure this out at 2AM while getting angry texts from people in different timezones. What chart of the system do you need? You need a high-level, far-away map of the entire system, and you need to know just enough to know where you need to dive in, where the monsters live , and you need to be able to jump into any unknown codebase, figure out what's happening, push a hotfix, and describe what happened clearly in your incident report.

Note that this is not detailed knowledge of the whole system. The only way we can manage complex systems is by building up abstractions. Each layer lets us build a bit more, but whatever map you have, it is important to remember that it is abstractions all the way down, and no one really understands all the layers. There is a big difference between "I wrote module X and know it inside out" and "I have an appropriate model of the system abstractions and can dive into any module and fix it when it breaks". Coding by hand gives us the former, but the owner of a system, the person who gets called, needs the latter.

items.title: Trump: 'Il partito del presidente non ottiene di solito buoni risultati alle midterm'
items.summary: 'Ma abbiamo girato in lungo e in largo, nessuno ha mai fatto campagna elettorale come me'
items.content:
"Abbiamo fatto il giro, abbiamo girato in lungo e in largo". Lo ha detto Donald Trump aprendo il suo comizio a Corinth, in Mississippi, riferendosi ai suoi numerosi spostamenti in tutto il Paese a sostegno dei repubblicani in vista delle midterm del 3 novembre. Il tycoon ha riconosciuto che, di solito, il partito del presidente "non ottiene buoni risultati" alle elezioni di metà mandato, ma ha aggiunto: "Nessuno ha mai fatto campagna elettorale come me per le elezioni di metà mandato". Il presidente americano è in Mississippi per sostenere la senatrice repubblicana Cindy Hyde-Smith sfidata dal democratico Scott Colom.

Trump, dal palco di Corinth, ha espresso la sua determinazione a invertire la tendenza storica per cui le elezioni di metà mandato si risolvono quasi sempre a sfavore del partito del presidente eletto due anni prima. Con voce roca, il tycoon ha sostenuto come i suoi comizi "abbiano cambiato completamente il dibattito" attorno alla campagna elettorale. "Per qualche motivo, i presidenti non ottengono buoni risultati alle elezioni di metà mandato, a prescindere da quanto siano bravi; anche se sono eccezionali, come noi", ha detto Trump. "Ma devo dire che nessuno ha mai fatto campagna elettorale, nessuno ha mai fatto campagna elettorale come ho fatto io in vista delle elezioni di metà mandato", ha ribadito il tycoon.

items.title: Apple presenta il nuovo iMac con M6: più potenza, Wi-Fi 7 e prezzi da 1.829 euro
items.summary: Apple aggiorna anche iMac da 24 pollici, che passa al nuovo chip M6
items.content:
Apple aggiorna anche iMac da 24 pollici, che passa al nuovo chip M6. Esteticamente non cambia praticamente nulla, a partire dal display Retina 4.5K. Rispetto alla versione con M4, oltre alle prestazioni, ci sono novità anche per l'archiviazione e la connettività, ora compatibile con Wi-Fi 7 e Bluetooth 6. Le colorazioni sono sempre le stesse: blu, verde, rosa, giallo, viola, arancione e argento. I prezzi partono da 1.829 euro, senza aumenti rispetto al modello M4. Per i preordini bisognerà attendere domani, mentre le prime consegne sono fissate per il 6 novembre.

CHIP M6, FINO A 12 CORE PER CPU E GPU

Con M6, Apple ha previsto due configurazioni per il nuovo iMac. Si parte da una CPU 10-core abbinata a una GPU 10-core, per arrivare a una versione superiore che dispone di 12 core per entrambe. In quest'ultimo caso ci sono quindi due core in più per CPU e GPU rispetto al precedente iMac M4.

I miglioramenti dichiarati da Apple riguardano diverse attività. Nell'utilizzo delle applicazioni di produttività si parla di prestazioni fino a 1,5 volte superiori rispetto a M4, mentre per l'elaborazione grafica e i giochi con ray tracing si può arrivare al doppio. Il confronto con gli iMac Intel è ancora più netto, con incrementi che in alcuni test raggiungono le 18 volte.

items.title: La nuova Dacia Sandero arriverà nel 2028: stile ancora più ricercato
items.summary: La prossima serie di Sandero risulterà ancora più curata. Valutiamo dai primi render le caratteristiche scelte da Dacia.
items.content:
La Casa romena sta ancora raccogliendo numeri importanti sul car market europeo con l'attuale generazione di Sandero, ma è già proiettata al futuro con una nuova idea di sviluppo. Serie dopo serie Dacia sta migliorando i suoi modelli sotto tutti gli aspetti, a partire da quello estetico. Attesa al lancio tra due anni, la nuova Sandero sarà una proposta chiave per l'intero Gruppo Renault.Pur rimanendo un'auto accessibile, la compatta di segmento B dovrà offrire soluzioni innovative per rimanere tra le scelte più popolare degli europei. Il marchio di Mioveni offrirà una strategia multi-energia che porterà al debutto anche la prima variante di Sandero full electric al fianco delle tradizionali versioni a combustione e ibride.

Nuovo linguaggio stilistico

Basandoci sulle foto del render di Sezer Car Design si può subito apprezzare una ricerca al dettaglio maggiore, puntando su un look più sportivo. L'obiettivo del responsabile del design David Durand sarà quello di offrire una Sandero con un frontale accattivante coordinato con gli ultimi modelli lanciati dal marchio romeno. Il profilo laterale risulta muscoloso come le sorelle maggiori, offrendo una varietà di linee tese e taglienti e dei gruppi ottici sottili a LED con la classica firma a "Y" evoluta e superfici geometriche.Le linee sinuose lasciano spazio a una interpretazione più netta, sempre orientando la scelta dei clienti su due distinte opzioni: Streetway e Stepway. Dacia ha assicurato che la variante da città (Streetway) e il crossover (Stepway) presenteranno un'identità stilistica più marcata rispetto alle attuali silhouette. La Stepway spiccherà per la sua forma da crossover con maggiore altezza da terra, protezioni in plastica riciclata Starkle e barre sul tetto. Le versioni termiche ed elettriche dovrebbero condividere un linguaggio stilistico comune.[gallery ids="292693,292694"]

Strategia Multi-Energia

Come stanno facendo anche tanti altri competitor, Dacia sfrutterà un'evoluzione della piattaforma CMF-B compatibile con diverse motorizzazioni, ma tanto dipenderà anche dalla crescita del car market green. I clienti apprezzeranno la possibilità di poter scegliere tra diverse tipologie di motori, ma le Case costruttrici devono anche riuscire a ottimizzare i costi industriali.Oltre alla versione 100% elettrica, saranno confermati i collaudati sistemi GPL e Mild-Hybrid e Full-Hybrid. L'autonomia stimata della batteria della variante elettrica intorno ai 300-350 km (WLTP), ideale per un uso quotidiano in città. Gli interni saranno sempre più moderni e in linea con la filosofia del "just needed", solo il necessario. Non mancherà l'uso di plastiche riciclate e tessuti lavabili, evitando finiture costose per privilegiare praticità e resistenza. Ne sapremo di più nel corso del 2027.

items.title: How Kane defied doubters to become world's best
items.summary: Harry Kane is the humble 'anti-superstar' who defied doubters to achieve Ballon d'Or greatness, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
items.content:
Harry Kane has taken the scenic route to the Ballon d'Or - a road littered with doubts and diversions, but one that eventually led to the ultimate destination: being crowned as the world's best player.

The 33-year-old's glory at the London Palladium on Monday is fitting reward for an exemplary career that has seen records fall at his feet for England, Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich.

Kane is England's top goalscorer with 91 goals. He has 125 England caps, joint-highest with Peter Shilton. He is Spurs' record scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances. He scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025–26 season.

This is the Kane of recent vintage, the world-class striker and complete footballer who beat Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe, as well as Spain's teenage Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, to the sport's biggest personal honour.

Kane's humility has seen him described as an 'anti-superstar' and his achievement has been commended both inside and outside the football world.

One post on social media from Kane as he celebrated the greatest moment of his career said it all: "Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise."

It was one that started with loan moves around the lower divisions with Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City before he developed into a great for club and country.

The same Kane sat on the bench on loan at Leicester City – alongside future England team-mate Jamie Vardy – when the Foxes lost a dramatic Championship play-off at Watford in May 2013.

Kane went through hard schools and hard times away from his more familiar environment at Spurs, joining Orient on loan as a 17-year-old in January 2011, playing 18 games with nine starts and scoring five goals.

He joined Millwall in similar circumstances a year later, with some behind the scenes at Spurs fearing the traditionally hostile atmosphere at the New Den might intimidate the teenager, but he acquitted himself well, scoring nine goals in 24 starts.

Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend

Tributes pour in as Kane wins Ballon d'Or - reaction & your views

Former Spurs manager Tim Sherwood said: "I used to watch Harry a lot at Millwall and it was an intimidating atmosphere. I remember overhearing one of our scouts come and talk to Harry Redknapp - who was Spurs manager at the time - and say: 'We need to get Harry Kane out of Millwall, it's no good for him there'.

"I went straight in and said: 'This is the perfect atmosphere for him'."

Kane made his Spurs debut in August 2012 before a spell at Norwich City, where he failed to score in three starts and suffered a serious foot injury.

It was an unhappy time but Chris Hughton, the former Spurs defender who was manager at Carrow Road, said: "What I saw in him was a desire to do well. Did I see him having the mobility and flexibility he has in his game now? Probably not. He was a very good finisher. He would stay out after training for half an hour every day, left foot, right foot."

Next stop was Leicester City between February and May 2013, when he made five starts and scored two goals, a stint best remembered for that dramatic Championship play-off game when Troy Deeney scored for Watford to send them to Wembley seconds after Anthony Knockaert's penalty was saved by Manuel Almunia.

Kane was not even selected in Leicester's starting line-up, only being sent on after 61 minutes. And who was alongside him on the bench? Vardy, who later won the Premier league with the Foxes and played alongside Kane for England.

He later admitted this was a time of self-doubt, saying: "That was probably the time in my career where it was the hardest - I was 19 and I was thinking, 'If I can't play for Norwich or for Leicester, even in the Championship, then how I am going to get back and play for Tottenham?'"

Ranking England's Ballon d'Or winners - how does Kane compare?

Quiz: Kane and who else? Name every men's Ballon d'Or winner

It is testimony to Kane's strength of character, even as a youngster, that he not only returned to Spurs but left for Bayern Munich in August 2023 as one of their greatest ever players.

Even at Spurs, Kane's superb record always carried the qualification that he never won a trophy, a stick used to unfairly beat a player whose remarkable consistency and approach marked him down as the consummate professional.

Kane has put that right spectacularly at Bayern, winning the Bundesliga twice, the move propelling him to the level of global superstar, giving him the profile and platform to win the Ballon d'Or - the first English player to win the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001 and the fifth overall.

Former England midfielder Danny Murphy told BBC Sport recently: "He's a born goalscorer. He's a super professional. He's technically brilliant. He's been an absolute credit to himself and his family in the way he's conducted himself and the longevity he's had in his career."

There is still that one space on his roll of honour, namely success with England after losses in two Euros finals and two World Cup semi-final defeats, but who would bet against Kane being fit and motivated enough to have one last crack at Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland.

Kane is now at the peak of his powers and fitness, not just a goalscoring machine but the complete player capable of dropping deep into midfield to play the sort of breathtaking defence splitting pass exemplified by Alphonso Davies' goal against Arsenal in the recent Champions League game.

One of Kane's illustrious predecessors in England's number nine shirt, Alan Shearer, told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was so well deserved because he hasn't had things all his own way. He's had to go round it the hard way. He had to start off the hard way by someone telling him, 'You're not quite good enough, you're going to have to work a lot harder to get to where you want to'.

"He did that. He went out on loan and worked harder than anyone else. He's got to the very, very top and now he's the best player in the world and that's what dedication does for you. It's a message to everyone.

"Harry said it in his speech - that if you're told you're not good enough, then go and try again and work harder. He did that and look where he is now. He's been scoring goals at a phenomenal rate for so many years now and he deserved it."

Shearer added: "I think the best thing for me is how humble Harry is. Footballers are like movie stars nowadays. You see them walking down the red carpet and some of them are in sunglasses when it's pitch black and eight o'clock at night. Harry is just normal, as normal as they come."

Once the celebrations die down, it will be back to business for the humble superstar, with Bayern playing Magdeburg in the German DFB Pokal second round on Wednesday before the big home fixture against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday evening.

Kane's career has not been without its obstacles but he remains as focused as ever to conquer whatever is placed in front of him by Bayern Munich and England.

items.title: Il mondo celebra Kane 'star senza lustrini', solo la Spagna non esulta
items.summary: 'Discreto e goleador creativo', l'inglese Pallone d'oro accontenta quasi tutti
items.content:
"Una superstar discreta e umile, un calciatore senza paillettes". Il mondo celebra Harry Kane, che dopo 25 anni riporta in Inghilterra il Pallone d'oro, interrompendo il digiuno che durava dal 2001 con l'ultima incoronazione di Michael Owen. Gli elogi al centravanti del Bayern Monaco e capitano della Nazionale dei Tre Leoni sono pressoché unanimi all'indomani della cerimonia al London Palladium, fatta eccezione per la Spagna che, nonostante abbia fatto incetta di premi, voleva che quello più ambito fosse assegnato al campione di casa Lamine Yamal o almeno al francese del Real Kilyan Mbappè, quest'ultimo rimasto ancora una volta a secco.

Tra i primi a incoronare il campione di casa è stato il principe William che ha definito Kane "capitano eccezionale" e "calciatore straordinario". Anche il ct dell'Inghilterra, il tedesco Thomas Tuchel, si è detto "entusiasta" per la vittoria di Kane, definendo il suo successo un "grande onore".

In festa i giornali britannici, con il Guardian che sottolinea "la fine di un'attesa durata venticinque anni per l'Inghilterra". Secondo il quotidiano "Kane ha meritato ampiamente di conquistare il trofeo calcistico più prestigioso.

Il premio corona un anno eccezionale: ha vinto la Scarpa d'Oro europea, ha giocato un ruolo chiave nella conquista del titolo di campione di Germania da parte del Bayern, ha trascinato l'Inghilterra fino alle semifinali ai Mondiali e, soprattutto, ha dimostrato un'umiltà straordinaria, pur essendo una superstar". Beniamino in Bundesliga "i 100 milioni di euro investiti sull'attaccante al momento del suo arrivo, tre anni fa - quando aveva già 30 anni - sono pienamente giustificati". In tanti sottolineano come "questo momento ha dimostrato che il calcio è capace di conferire i massimi riconoscimenti a uomini come lui, che non hanno cercato né la gloria né la polemica".

Gioco di parole sul Sun che titola "Yes he Kan!". Il Daily Mail parla della "consacrazione per una superstar che trabocca di discrezione e che si tiene alla larga dalle polemiche". Un giocatore "che non ha abusato della propria celebrità e che, a differenza di Yamal, si è dedicato a una carriera all'insegna di un'eccellenza discreta. La vittoria di Kane è quella di un giocatore privo del narcisismo esuberante, che incarna un professionismo esemplare". "Un goleador creativo, sottolineano molti. Dalla pioggia di consensi si sfila la Spagna: lo zio di Yamal parte in causa contesta la scelta: "A Kane restano tre giorni di calcio nelle gambe, e noi gli diamo il premio", sottolineando che suo nipote (premiato come top giovane) "è il migliore al mondo".

Ma la giuria ha scelto Kane e ancora una volta lasciato senza riconoscimento Mbappè: e l'inglese ha condiviso il premio "con le sue squadre" (il Bayern e la nazionale inglese), di cui si dice onorato di vestire le maglie. "E' stato un anno speciale, direi perfetto" ha detto il nuovo Pallone d'oro.

items.title: Co-ordinated cattle raids kill at least 72 people in South Sudan
items.summary: The cycle of revenge attacks continue as the country heads towards its first election since independence.
items.content:
At least 72 people have been killed during cattle raids in South Sudan's northern Warrap state, according to the regional government.

An unspecified number of cattle were taken and homes burnt during what was a "co-ordinated attack" on Monday involving two communities in Tonj North county, the state authorities said.

Such deadly violence is often part of a cycle of revenge attacks as cattle are a main source of wealth and pride for many communities and are also important as young men need them as dowries to get married.

Clashes over territory are also common across the country as it prepares to hold its first election since its independence in 2011 - delayed because of a brutal civil war.

The clashes occurred near the border of Warrap and Unity states in the area of Akop Payam, with some members from Lou Ariik community said to have attacked those from Apuk Padoch community.

William Wol Mayom Bol, Warrap state's information minister, said they followed deadly violence last Friday that claimed eight lives.

The state governor, Angelo Ngot Mayar, sent his condolences to bereaved families and directed security agencies to evacuate the wounded.

He said efforts were under way recover the cattle and find those behind the assault.

The state has also appealed to humanitarian partners to support vulnerable women, children and elderly left without food, shelter and medicine.

In August, at least 60 people were killed and 50 injured in an attack in the same area of Warrap state, according to Acled, the non-profit conflict monitoring group.

Last year, a six-month state of emergency was declared in Warrup in efforts to quell the increasing violence.

The UN has also voiced its concerns about the situation in South Sudan as the world's youngest country heads towards presidential elections due to be held in December .

The poll was initially delayed by the civil war, which ended in 2018 with a fragile peace deal signed between President Salva Kiir and his deputy Riek Machar.

However tensions between the leaders led to further delays: Machar was sacked as vice-president and arrested earlier last year and charged with murder, treason and crimes against humanity, which he denies.

He has been under house arrest in the capital, Juba, since March last year as fighting persists in some areas of the country.

Preparations for the elections have lagged and human rights groups have raised questions over whether the country can complete key things like voter registration and security arrangements before the vote.
